Connectivity
Japan

ప్రధాన రంగాలు:

Infrastructure
Technology
Indo-Pacific
Economic Cooperation
Australia

ప్రధాన రంగాలు:

QUAD
Indo-Pacific
Critical Minerals
Trade
Defence
Education
12. India's Foreign Policy — ముఖ్యమైన Themes

2025 భారత విదేశాంగ విధానాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకోవడానికి ఈ అంశాలు ముఖ్యమైనవి.

Strategic Autonomy

భారతదేశం తన జాతీయ ప్రయోజనాలను దృష్టిలో ఉంచుకుని స్వతంత్రంగా నిర్ణయాలు తీసుకునే సామర్థ్యాన్ని కొనసాగించడం.

Multilateralism

భారత్:

BRICS
SCO
QUAD
G20
United Nations

వంటి అంతర్జాతీయ వేదికల్లో చురుకుగా పాల్గొంటుంది.

Global South

అభివృద్ధి చెందుతున్న దేశాల సమస్యలకు ప్రాధాన్యత ఇవ్వడం.

Counter-Terrorism

2025లో Pahalgam దాడి తరువాత counter-terrorism భారత విదేశాంగంలో ముఖ్యమైన అంశంగా నిలిచింది.

Technology Diplomacy

AI, Semiconductors, Space, Digital Public Infrastructure మరియు Cybersecurity వంటి రంగాలు విదేశాంగ సంబంధాల్లో కూడా ముఖ్యమైనవిగా మారాయి.

13. United Nations Reform

భారతదేశం చాలాకాలంగా United Nations Security Council reformకు మద్దతు ఇస్తోంది.

భద్రతా మండలిలో:

Permanent Membership
Non-Permanent Membership

రెండింటిలోనూ ప్రాతినిధ్యం విస్తరించాలని భారత్ కోరుతోంది.

భారతదేశం అభిప్రాయం ప్రకారం ప్రస్తుత అంతర్జాతీయ సంస్థలు నేటి ప్రపంచంలోని దేశాల వాస్తవ ప్రాతినిధ్యాన్ని ప్రతిబింబించేలా మరింత representativeగా ఉండాలి.

title: Major Constitutional, Legal & Governance Developments
title_te: ముఖ్యమైన రాజ్యాంగ, న్యాయ మరియు పాలనా పరిణామాలు
description:
Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026

One of the important legal-reform developments of 2026 is the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026.

The reform continues the approach started by the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023, which aimed to reduce criminal penalties for minor and technical violations.

The 2026 Act amended provisions across 79 Central Acts administered by 23 Ministries and Departments. It dealt with 784 provisions, including the decriminalisation of 717 provisions and amendments to another 67 provisions. The Act came into effect on 7 April 2026.

The basic idea is to replace criminal punishment for certain minor procedural violations with civil penalties, warnings or administrative mechanisms, while retaining stricter provisions for serious offences.

Importance:
It is connected with:

Ease of Doing Business
Ease of Living
Reduction of unnecessary criminalisation
Simplification of compliance
Trust-based governance
2. Repealing and Amending Act, 2025 – Implemented in 2026

The Repealing and Amending Act, 2025 is another important legal-clean-up measure relevant to 2026.

It removed 71 obsolete or redundant Central Acts from the statute book. It also made targeted amendments to certain existing laws to correct inconsistencies and improve legal clarity.

The purpose of such legislation is to keep the legal system updated by removing laws that are no longer required.

Exam point:
Remember the number 71.

3. Increase in Supreme Court Judge Strength

In May 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a proposal to increase the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, excluding the Chief Justice of India. This means an increase of 4 judges.

The proposal was taken forward through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026.

The objective stated by the government was to improve the Court's capacity and help in the more efficient and speedy disposal of cases.

4. Tribunals Reforms

The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 was among the important legislative measures passed by both Houses during the 2026 Monsoon Session.

The Bill seeks to improve:

Efficiency of tribunals
Independence
Transparency
Uniformity in qualifications and appointments
Terms and conditions of tribunal members

It also proposes a National Tribunals Commission for administration and functioning of tribunals.

5. Public Examinations and Prevention of Unfair Means

The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced and passed during the 2026 Monsoon Session. It relates to strengthening the legal framework governing unfair practices in public examinations.

This is particularly important for competitive-exam aspirants because it concerns examination integrity and measures against unfair means.

6. Registration of Births and Deaths

The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026 was also passed by both Houses during the Monsoon Session.

The registration system is important because birth and death records form a major part of official demographic and administrative databases.

7. One Nation, One Election

The proposal for simultaneous elections, commonly referred to as One Nation, One Election, continued to be examined in 2026.

A Joint Committee was examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.

During 2026, the committee conducted consultations with legislators, officials, experts and other stakeholders. Issues discussed included:

Premature dissolution of legislatures
Mid-term elections
Tenure of legislatures
Role of the Election Commission
Federalism
Basic Structure Doctrine

Important: As of the cited 2026 developments, this should be understood as a constitutional and legislative proposal under examination, not as a completed nationwide simultaneous-election system.

8. 2026 Monsoon Session of Parliament

The Monsoon Session of Parliament 2026 began on 20 July 2026 and concluded on 13 August 2026.

According to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs:

19 sittings were held over 25 days.
11 Bills were introduced in Lok Sabha.
2 Bills were introduced in Rajya Sabha.
12 Bills were passed by both Houses.

Important legislation included:

Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill
Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill
Registration of Births and Deaths Amendment Bill
Tribunals Reforms Bill
Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill
Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill
MSME Development Amendment Bill
description_te:
Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026

2026లో ముఖ్యమైన న్యాయ సంస్కరణల్లో Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2026 ఒకటి.

ఇది 2023లో ప్రారంభమైన Jan Vishwas సంస్కరణలను కొనసాగిస్తుంది.

2026 చట్టం ద్వారా 23 మంత్రిత్వ శాఖలు/శాఖలకు సంబంధించిన 79 కేంద్ర చట్టాల్లో 784 నిబంధనలను మార్చారు.

అందులో 717 నిబంధనలను decriminalise చేశారు. అంటే చిన్నపాటి లేదా సాంకేతిక తప్పిదాలకు క్రిమినల్ శిక్షల స్థానంలో సివిల్ పెనాల్టీలు, హెచ్చరికలు లేదా పరిపాలనా చర్యలను ఉపయోగించే విధంగా మార్పులు చేశారు.

ఈ చట్టం 7 ఏప్రిల్ 2026 నుంచి అమల్లోకి వచ్చింది.

ముఖ్య ఉద్దేశాలు:

Ease of Doing Business
Ease of Living
చిన్న తప్పిదాల criminalisation తగ్గించడం
Compliance burden తగ్గించడం
Trust-based governance
2. Repealing and Amending Act, 2025

2026లో అమలులోకి వచ్చిన మరో ముఖ్యమైన న్యాయ సంస్కరణ Repealing and Amending Act, 2025.

దీని ద్వారా 71 పాత, అవసరం లేని లేదా obsolete Central Acts చట్టపుస్తకం నుంచి తొలగించబడ్డాయి. అలాగే కొన్ని ప్రస్తుత చట్టాల్లో సాంకేతిక మార్పులు చేసి చట్టపరమైన స్పష్టతను పెంచారు.

Exam Point:
👉 71 obsolete Acts

3. Supreme Court న్యాయమూర్తుల సంఖ్య పెంపు

2026 మేలో Union Cabinet, Supreme Court న్యాయమూర్తుల sanctioned strength‌ను 33 నుంచి 37కి పెంచే ప్రతిపాదనకు ఆమోదం తెలిపింది.

Chief Justice of India ఇందులో లెక్కించబడరు.

అంటే 4 మంది న్యాయమూర్తుల పెంపు.

దీని ప్రధాన ఉద్దేశ్యం కేసుల పరిష్కార సామర్థ్యాన్ని పెంచడం మరియు న్యాయ ప్రక్రియను మరింత సమర్థవంతంగా నిర్వహించడం.

4. Tribunals Reforms

2026 Monsoon Sessionలో Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 ముఖ్యమైన బిల్లులలో ఒకటి.

దీని ప్రధాన అంశాలు:

Tribunals సామర్థ్యం పెంపు
స్వతంత్రత
పారదర్శకత
నియామకాలలో ఏకరీతి
సభ్యుల అర్హతలు మరియు సేవా నిబంధనల్లో uniformity

అలాగే National Tribunals Commission ఏర్పాటుకు సంబంధించిన ప్రతిపాదన కూడా ఉంది.

5. Public Examinations – Unfair Means

Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 కూడా 2026లో ముఖ్యమైన న్యాయ పరిణామం.

ప్రభుత్వ నియంత్రణలో జరిగే పరీక్షల్లో:

unfair means
cheating
examination integrity

వంటి అంశాలను నియంత్రించడానికి చట్టపరమైన వ్యవస్థను బలోపేతం చేయడం దీని లక్ష్యం.

Competitive-exam aspirants‌కు ఇది ముఖ్యమైన current-affairs topic.

6. Births and Deaths Registration

Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Bill, 2026 కూడా Parliamentలో ఆమోదం పొందింది.

జననాలు, మరణాల అధికారిక రికార్డులు జనాభా గణాంకాలు మరియు ప్రభుత్వ పరిపాలనలో చాలా ముఖ్యమైనవి.

7. One Nation, One Election

One Nation, One Election అంటే దేశంలో Lok Sabha మరియు State Legislative Assembly ఎన్నికలను ఒకే ఎన్నికల చక్రంలో నిర్వహించాలనే ప్రతిపాదన.

2026లో ఈ అంశంపై Joint Committee పరిశీలన మరియు stakeholder consultations కొనసాగాయి.

చర్చించిన అంశాలు:

Assembly ముందుగానే రద్దయితే?
Mid-term elections ఎలా?
మిగిలిన పదవీకాలం ఎలా?
Election Commission పాత్ర
Federalism
Basic Structure Doctrine

ముఖ్యమైన విషయం: 2026లో ఇది ఇంకా పరిశీలనలో ఉన్న రాజ్యాంగ/శాసన ప్రతిపాదనగా అర్థం చేసుకోవాలి; దేశవ్యాప్తంగా simultaneous elections ఇప్పటికే అమల్లోకి వచ్చాయని భావించకూడదు.

8. 2026 Monsoon Session

2026 Parliament Monsoon Session 20 July 2026 నుంచి 13 August 2026 వరకు జరిగింది.

మొత్తం:

19 sittings
25 రోజులు
Lok Sabhaలో 11 Bills introduced
Rajya Sabhaలో 2 Bills introduced
12 Bills రెండు సభల ద్వారా ఆమోదం పొందాయి.

ముఖ్యమైనవి:

Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill
Public Examinations Amendment Bill
Registration of Births and Deaths Amendment Bill
Tribunals Reforms Bill
Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill
Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill
MSME Development Amendment Bill

title: Environment, Climate Change & Renewable Energy
description:
India’s Non-Fossil Capacity Crosses 300 GW

A major milestone was achieved in 2026, when India crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil-fuel electricity capacity.

As of 31 July 2026, India had 300.50 GW of non-fossil capacity, representing more than 54% of total installed electricity capacity.

The breakup was:

Solar – 164.59 GW
Wind – 58.14 GW
Hydro – 57.24 GW
Bio-power – 11.75 GW
Nuclear – 8.78 GW

India's total installed power capacity was around 552 GW at that time.

This is significant because India has a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity capacity by 2030.

2. India Achieves the 50% Non-Fossil Electricity Capacity Target Early

Under India's climate commitments, one important target was to achieve 50% cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.

India crossed this level in June 2025, five years ahead of the original target.

By 30 June 2026, non-fossil sources accounted for 54.18% of India's total installed electricity capacity.

This includes solar, wind, hydro and nuclear power.

Exam point:
👉 India's 50% non-fossil installed-capacity target was achieved five years ahead of schedule.

3. India’s New NDC for 2031–2035

One of the most important climate-policy developments of 2026 was the Union Cabinet's approval of India's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) for 2031–2035 on 25 March 2026.

India committed to:

1. Reduce emissions intensity of GDP by 47% by 2035, compared with the 2005 level.

2. Achieve 60% cumulative installed electric-power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2035.

3. Create an additional carbon sink of 3.5–4.0 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent through forest and tree cover by 2035, compared with 2005.

These targets are aligned with India's broader Viksit Bharat @2047 vision and its commitment to achieving Net Zero emissions by 2070.

4. India’s Progress on Existing Climate Targets

India reported significant progress toward its existing NDC targets.

As of the latest government figures:

Emissions intensity of GDP had declined by 37.38% in 2022 from the 2005 level.
Non-fossil sources crossed 50% of installed electricity capacity in June 2025.
India had created an additional carbon sink of approximately 2.44 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent during 2005–2022.

The existing 2030 targets include:

45% reduction in emissions intensity from 2005 level.
50% cumulative installed electric power capacity from non-fossil sources.
Additional carbon sink of 2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent.
5. Renewable Energy Capacity Reaches Nearly 289 GW

India's renewable-energy capacity continued to expand rapidly.

As of 30 June 2026, installed renewable-energy capacity was 288.58 GW.

Breakup:

Solar – 162.15 GW
Wind – 57.44 GW
Bio-power – 11.75 GW
Hydro – 57.24 GW

Including nuclear, total non-fossil capacity was 297.36 GW at that point.

By 31 August 2026, MNRE reported total renewable capacity of approximately 295.55 GW and total non-fossil capacity of 304.33 GW.

6. National Green Hydrogen Mission

India continued implementing the National Green Hydrogen Mission, launched in 2023.

Green hydrogen is produced using renewable electricity and can help decarbonise sectors where direct electrification is difficult, such as:

Steel
Fertilizers
Chemicals
Heavy transport
Shipping

The mission aims to establish India as a major producer and exporter of green hydrogen while developing a domestic manufacturing ecosystem.

7. GOBARdhan and Circular Bioeconomy

In August 2026, the government approved the GOBARdhan – National Circular Bioenergy Scheme.

It has an outlay of approximately ₹23,731 crore for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36.

The scheme focuses on converting organic waste and agricultural waste into useful energy products such as Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG)/Bio-CNG.

As of August 2026, 1,929 CBG/Bio-CNG plants had been registered, with 217 commissioned and 357 under construction.

GOBARdhan = Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan.

8. Small Hydro Power Development Scheme

The government approved the Small Hydro Power Development Scheme in March 2026.

It covers FY 2026–27 to FY 2030–31 and has an outlay of approximately ₹2,584.60 crore.

Its objective is to add around 1,500 MW of small-hydro capacity, particularly supporting projects in hilly and North-Eastern areas.

9. Renewable Energy and Grid Infrastructure

As solar and wind capacity increases, India needs a stronger electricity transmission network.

The government has therefore been expanding:

Inter-State Transmission Systems
Intra-State Transmission Systems
Green Energy Corridors
Energy-storage systems
Smart-grid technology
Long-distance HVDC transmission

Transmission planning has been undertaken to integrate more than 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030.
description_te:
Non-Fossil Capacity 300 GW దాటింది

31 July 2026 నాటికి భారతదేశం 300.50 GW non-fossil electricity capacityను చేరుకుంది.

ఇది దేశ మొత్తం installed electricity capacityలో 54% కంటే ఎక్కువ.

విభజన:

Solar – 164.59 GW
Wind – 58.14 GW
Hydro – 57.24 GW
Bio-power – 11.75 GW
Nuclear – 8.78 GW

భారతదేశం 2030 నాటికి 500 GW non-fossil capacity సాధించాలనే లక్ష్యంతో ముందుకు వెళ్తోంది.

2. 50% Non-Fossil Target ముందుగానే సాధన

భారతదేశం 2030 నాటికి installed electricity capacityలో 50% non-fossil sources నుంచి రావాలనే climate target పెట్టుకుంది.

ఈ లక్ష్యాన్ని భారత్ June 2025లోనే సాధించింది.

అంటే నిర్ణయించిన సమయానికి 5 సంవత్సరాల ముందుగానే ఈ లక్ష్యాన్ని చేరుకుంది.

30 June 2026 నాటికి non-fossil sources వాటా **54.18%**గా ఉంది.

3. 2031–2035 కోసం కొత్త NDC

25 March 2026న Union Cabinet, భారత్‌కు సంబంధించిన 2031–2035 NDCని ఆమోదించింది.

ముఖ్యమైన లక్ష్యాలు:

1. 2035 నాటికి 2005 స్థాయితో పోలిస్తే GDP emissions intensityను 47% తగ్గించడం.

2. 2035 నాటికి cumulative installed electric power capacityలో 60% non-fossil sources నుంచి సాధించడం.

3. Forest మరియు tree cover ద్వారా 3.5–4.0 billion tonnes CO₂ equivalent carbon sink సృష్టించడం.

ఈ లక్ష్యాలు Viksit Bharat @2047 మరియు Net Zero by 2070 లక్ష్యాలతో అనుసంధానించబడ్డాయి.

4. ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న Climate Targetsలో పురోగతి

భారతదేశం ఇప్పటికే కొన్ని climate targetsలో మంచి పురోగతి సాధించింది.

2022 నాటికి GDP emissions intensity 37.38% తగ్గింది.
June 2025లో non-fossil installed capacity 50% దాటింది.
2005–2022 మధ్య సుమారు 2.44 billion tonnes CO₂ equivalent carbon sink సృష్టించబడింది.
5. Renewable Energy Capacity

30 June 2026 నాటికి భారతదేశ renewable energy capacity 288.58 GW.

విభజన:

Solar – 162.15 GW
Wind – 57.44 GW
Bio-power – 11.75 GW
Hydro – 57.24 GW

31 August 2026 నాటికి MNRE ప్రకారం renewable capacity సుమారు 295.55 GW, మొత్తం non-fossil capacity 304.33 GWకు చేరింది.

6. National Green Hydrogen Mission

భారతదేశం National Green Hydrogen Missionను కొనసాగిస్తోంది.

Green hydrogenను renewable electricity ఉపయోగించి ఉత్పత్తి చేస్తారు.

ఇది ముఖ్యంగా:

Steel
Fertilizers
Chemicals
Heavy transport
Shipping

వంటి రంగాల్లో carbon emissions తగ్గించడానికి ఉపయోగపడుతుంది.

భారతదేశాన్ని green hydrogen ఉత్పత్తి మరియు exportలో ముఖ్యమైన దేశంగా అభివృద్ధి చేయడం దీని ప్రధాన లక్ష్యాలలో ఒకటి.

7. GOBARdhan – National Circular Bioenergy Scheme

August 2026లో ప్రభుత్వం GOBARdhan – National Circular Bioenergy Schemeను ఆమోదించింది.

దీనికి ₹23,731 crore outlay ఉంది.

ఇది FY 2026–27 నుంచి FY 2035–36 వరకు అమలులో ఉంటుంది.

వ్యవసాయ వ్యర్థాలు మరియు organic wasteను ఉపయోగించి Compressed Bio-Gas (CBG)/Bio-CNG వంటి energy products తయారు చేయడం దీని ముఖ్య ఉద్దేశ్యం.

GOBARdhan = Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan

8. Small Hydro Power Development Scheme

March 2026లో Small Hydro Power Development Schemeకు ప్రభుత్వం ఆమోదం తెలిపింది.

కాలవ్యవధి:

FY 2026–27 నుంచి FY 2030–31

Outlay:

₹2,584.60 crore

లక్ష్యం:

సుమారు 1,500 MW small-hydro capacityను పెంచడం, ముఖ్యంగా hilly మరియు North-Eastern ప్రాంతాల్లో.

9. Renewable Energy కోసం Grid Infrastructure

Solar, wind capacity పెరుగుతున్నందున renewable electricityను దేశవ్యాప్తంగా పంపిణీ చేయడానికి బలమైన transmission network అవసరం.

అందుకే ప్రభుత్వం:

Green Energy Corridors
Inter-State Transmission Systems
Intra-State Transmission Systems
Energy Storage
Smart Grid
HVDC transmission

వంటి వ్యవస్థలను అభివృద్ధి చేస్తోంది.

2030 నాటికి 500 GW కంటే ఎక్కువ renewable capacityను gridలో integrate చేయడానికి transmission planning జరుగుతోంది.

title: Health, Education & Social Development
description:
Ayushman Bharat and Healthcare Expansion

India continued strengthening Ayushman Bharat, particularly through the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and Ayushman Arogya Mandirs.

The broader objective is to make healthcare more accessible through:

Primary healthcare
Preventive healthcare
Digital health records
Telemedicine
Health insurance/financial protection
Maternal and child healthcare

Exam point:
Ayushman Bharat has two major components:

PM-JAY → financial protection for eligible families for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation.

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs → comprehensive primary healthcare closer to communities.

2. Digital Health and ABHA

The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) continued expanding India's digital-health ecosystem.

Its important component is the ABHA – Ayushman Bharat Health Account.

ABHA enables individuals to maintain and access their digital health records through a unique health-account framework.

The larger objective is interoperability between:

Hospitals
Laboratories
Doctors
Pharmacies
Patients

This is important for India's transition toward a more connected digital healthcare system.

3. National Education Policy 2020 – Continued Implementation

The implementation of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 remained an important education-development area.

The NEP introduced the 5+3+3+4 curricular structure, replacing the earlier 10+2 structure.

It focuses on:

Foundational Literacy and Numeracy
Multidisciplinary education
Skill development
Vocational education
Indian languages
Digital education
Flexible higher education
Multiple entry and exit options
Research and innovation

The Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) allows students' academic credits to be digitally stored and transferred between participating institutions.

4. Foundational Literacy and Numeracy

Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) continues to be one of the central priorities under NEP 2020.

The government's NIPUN Bharat Mission focuses on ensuring that children acquire basic reading, writing and numeracy skills during the foundational stage.

The basic idea is:

Strong foundational learning → better school education → improved learning outcomes.

This is particularly important for primary-school education.

5. Skill Development and Employment

Skill development continued to be an important component of India's social-development strategy.

Major areas include:

Vocational education
Apprenticeships
Digital skills
Industry-linked training
Entrepreneurship
New-age technology skills

The emphasis is increasingly shifting toward skills related to:

Artificial Intelligence
Semiconductor technology
Robotics
Cybersecurity
Electronics
Green technologies

This connects education with India's changing employment requirements.

6. Women and Child Development

Government programmes continued to focus on women's economic participation, nutrition and child development.

Important areas include:

Mission Shakti

Women’s safety
Women’s empowerment
Support services

Mission Vatsalya

Child protection
Child welfare
Institutional and non-institutional care

Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN 2.0

Nutrition
Early childhood care
Anganwadi services
Health and developmental support

These programmes are important for questions relating to women and child welfare.

7. Nutrition and POSHAN

Nutrition remains an important social-development indicator.

POSHAN Abhiyaan focuses on reducing:

Malnutrition
Anaemia
Low birth weight
Stunting
Wasting

POSHAN 2.0 integrates several nutrition-related interventions and focuses particularly on:

Children
Pregnant women
Lactating mothers
Adolescent girls
8. PM-JANMAN and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups

The government continued implementing PM-JANMAN – Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan.

It focuses specifically on the development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).

The programme covers areas such as:

Housing
Drinking water
Sanitation
Education
Health
Electricity
Roads
Telecommunications
Sustainable livelihoods

Important exam point:
👉 PM-JANMAN = PVTGs

9. Aspirational Districts and Blocks

The Aspirational Districts Programme, implemented by NITI Aayog, continued to focus on improving development indicators in relatively underdeveloped districts.

The programme uses measurable indicators in areas such as:

Health and nutrition
Education
Agriculture
Financial inclusion
Basic infrastructure

The Aspirational Blocks Programme extends this approach to selected blocks.

The broader concept is outcome-based development rather than simply measuring expenditure.

10. Social Security and Inclusion

Social-development programmes in 2026 continued to focus on inclusion of vulnerable sections.

Important areas include:

Financial inclusion
Social security
Housing
Rural employment
Food security
Health protection
Disability support
Senior-citizen welfare
Tribal development

Digital public infrastructure such as Aadhaar, DBT and Jan Dhan accounts continues to support the delivery of welfare benefits.
description_te:
Ayushman Bharat మరియు ఆరోగ్య సేవలు

2026లో భారతదేశం Ayushman Bharat కార్యక్రమం ద్వారా healthcare accessను మరింత బలోపేతం చేయడంపై దృష్టి కొనసాగించింది.

ముఖ్యమైన అంశాలు:

Primary healthcare
Preventive healthcare
Digital health records
Telemedicine
Health insurance
తల్లి మరియు శిశు ఆరోగ్యం

Ayushman Bharatలో ముఖ్యంగా రెండు ప్రధాన భాగాలను గుర్తుంచుకోవాలి:

PM-JAY → అర్హత కలిగిన కుటుంబాలకు secondary మరియు tertiary hospitalisation కోసం ఆర్థిక రక్షణ.

Ayushman Arogya Mandirs → ప్రజలకు సమీపంలో comprehensive primary healthcare అందించడం.

2. Digital Health మరియు ABHA

Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) ద్వారా భారతదేశంలో digital-health ecosystem అభివృద్ధి కొనసాగుతోంది.

దీనిలో ముఖ్యమైనది:

ABHA – Ayushman Bharat Health Account

దీని ద్వారా వ్యక్తుల health recordsను digital రూపంలో నిర్వహించడానికి మరియు అవసరమైనప్పుడు access చేయడానికి వీలు ఉంటుంది.

ఇది:

Hospitals
Laboratories
Doctors
Pharmacies
Patients

మధ్య digital connectivityను మెరుగుపరచడానికి ఉపయోగపడుతుంది.

3. National Education Policy 2020 అమలు

2026లో కూడా NEP 2020 implementation ముఖ్యమైన education-development అంశంగా కొనసాగుతోంది.

NEPలో ముఖ్యమైన 5+3+3+4 curricular structure ఉంది.

ఇది పాత 10+2 విధానానికి భిన్నమైన నిర్మాణం.

ముఖ్యమైన అంశాలు:

Foundational Literacy and Numeracy
Multidisciplinary education
Skill development
Vocational education
Indian languages
Digital education
Flexible higher education
Multiple entry and exit
Research and innovation

Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ద్వారా విద్యార్థుల academic creditsను digital రూపంలో నిల్వ చేసి, institutions మధ్య transfer చేయవచ్చు.

4. Foundational Literacy and Numeracy

NEP 2020లో Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) చాలా ముఖ్యమైన అంశం.

దీనికి సంబంధించిన ముఖ్యమైన కార్యక్రమం:

NIPUN Bharat Mission

దీని లక్ష్యం పిల్లలకు foundational stageలోనే:

Reading
Writing
Basic Mathematics

పై బలమైన పునాది కల్పించడం.

Exam Point:
👉 NIPUN Bharat = Foundational Literacy and Numeracy

5. Skill Development మరియు Employment

2026లో skill development కూడా ముఖ్యమైన సామాజిక అభివృద్ధి అంశంగా కొనసాగుతోంది.

ముఖ్యమైన రంగాలు:

Vocational education
Apprenticeships
Digital skills
Industry-linked training
Entrepreneurship

కొత్తగా ప్రాధాన్యం పొందుతున్న skills:

Artificial Intelligence
Semiconductor technology
Robotics
Cybersecurity
Electronics
Green technology

దీని ప్రధాన ఉద్దేశ్యం education మరియు employment మధ్య సంబంధాన్ని బలోపేతం చేయడం.

6. Women and Child Development

మహిళలు మరియు పిల్లల అభివృద్ధికి సంబంధించిన పథకాలు కూడా ముఖ్యమైనవి.

Mission Shakti

మహిళల భద్రత
మహిళా సాధికారత
Support services

Mission Vatsalya

Child protection
Child welfare
పిల్లల సంరక్షణ

Saksham Anganwadi & POSHAN 2.0

Nutrition
Early childhood care
Anganwadi services
Child development
7. POSHAN మరియు Nutrition

భారతదేశంలో malnutritionను తగ్గించడం సామాజిక అభివృద్ధిలో ముఖ్యమైన అంశం.

POSHAN Abhiyaan ప్రధానంగా:

Malnutrition
Anaemia
Low birth weight
Stunting
Wasting

వంటి సమస్యలను తగ్గించడంపై దృష్టి పెడుతుంది.

POSHAN 2.0 ముఖ్యంగా:

పిల్లలు
గర్భిణీలు
పాలిచ్చే తల్లులు
Adolescent girls

పై దృష్టి పెడుతుంది.

8. PM-JANMAN

PM-JANMAN = Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan

ఇది ముఖ్యంగా Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) అభివృద్ధి కోసం రూపొందించబడింది.

ముఖ్యమైన రంగాలు:

Housing
Drinking water
Sanitation
Education
Health
Electricity
Roads
Telecommunications
Livelihoods

Exam Point:
👉 PM-JANMAN → PVTGs

9. Aspirational Districts & Aspirational Blocks

Aspirational Districts Programmeను NITI Aayog అమలు చేస్తోంది.

ఇది అభివృద్ధిలో వెనుకబడిన జిల్లాల్లో measurable improvement తీసుకురావడానికి ఉద్దేశించబడింది.

ప్రధాన రంగాలు:

Health & Nutrition
Education
Agriculture
Financial Inclusion
Infrastructure

Aspirational Blocks Programme ఇదే విధానాన్ని selected blocks స్థాయికి తీసుకువెళ్తుంది.

ముఖ్యమైన భావన:

Outcome-based development

10. Social Security మరియు Inclusion

2026లో కూడా vulnerable sections కోసం social-development programmes కొనసాగుతున్నాయి.

ముఖ్యమైన రంగాలు:

Financial inclusion
Social security
Housing
Rural employment
Food security
Health protection
Disability support
Senior citizens welfare
Tribal development

Aadhaar + Jan Dhan + DBT వంటి digital public infrastructure వ్యవస్థలు welfare benefitsను నేరుగా లబ్ధిదారులకు చేరవేయడంలో ఉపయోగపడుతున్నాయి.

title: Sports & Major Sporting Events
description:
Commonwealth Games 2026 – Glasgow

The Commonwealth Games 2026 were held in Glasgow, Scotland, from 23 July to 2 August 2026.

The Games featured athletes from 74 countries across a 10-sport programme, including six integrated para-sports. India participated with a 124-member contingent.

India finished fourth in the overall medal table, winning:

13 Gold
17 Silver
9 Bronze
39 Total Medals

This was India's medal tally at the completed Games.

2. Mirabai Chanu – Historic Commonwealth Achievement

Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won gold at Glasgow 2026.

This was particularly significant because it was her third consecutive Commonwealth Games title.

Exam Point:

👉 Mirabai Chanu = Three consecutive Commonwealth Games titles

3. Indian Boxing Performance

India had a strong campaign in boxing at Glasgow.

Indian boxers won:

7 Gold
3 Silver
10 Total Medals

India topped the boxing medal tally.

The seven gold medals also represented India's best-ever performance by women boxers at the Commonwealth Games.

4. Indian Judo Performance

Indian judokas produced India's best-ever Commonwealth Games performance in judo.

India won:

2 Gold
1 Silver
1 Bronze
4 Total Medals

Asmita Dey and Harsh Singh won India's first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medals in judo.

Asmita Dey became the first Indian woman judoka to win Commonwealth Games gold, while Harsh Singh became the first Indian male judoka to achieve the feat.

5. Commonwealth Games Weightlifting

Indian weightlifters won 8 medals at Glasgow:

1 Gold
6 Silver
1 Bronze

Indian weightlifters also recorded several Commonwealth Games records and personal-best performances.

6. Commonwealth Para Games 2026

India's para-athletes also delivered a notable performance.

India won:

3 Gold
2 Silver
2 Bronze
7 Total Medals

This was India's best-ever performance at the Commonwealth Para Games.

7. Asian Games 2026 – Aichi-Nagoya

The 20th Asian Games are being held in Japan from 19 September to 4 October 2026.

The host region is Aichi-Nagoya.

India sent a 503-member contingent, with more than 300 athletes making their first Asian Games appearance.

This makes the 2026 Asian Games one of the major sporting events for Indian current affairs.

8. Jay Meena – Historic Soft Tennis Medal

A notable Indian achievement at the 2026 Asian Games was recorded by Jay Meena.

He won bronze in the men's individual soft tennis event.

This made him India's first-ever Asian Games medallist in soft tennis.

Exam Point:

👉 Jay Meena → First Indian Asian Games medallist in Soft Tennis

9. Khelo India – Major Expansion

In July 2026, the Union Cabinet approved an expanded Khelo India Scheme and enhanced assistance to National Sports Federations.

The combined outlay is ₹36,441 crore for 2026–27 to 2030–31.

The programme aims to strengthen:

Sports infrastructure
Athlete development
Grassroots sports
Talent identification
Training facilities
National sports federations
10. KIRTI – Talent Identification

KIRTI stands for:

Khelo India Rising Talent Identification

It focuses on identifying and developing young sporting talent between 9 and 18 years.

The programme uses Talent Assessment Centres and technology including AI and data analytics.

As of 2026, 174 Talent Assessment Centres were operating across three States/UTs, with 1,87,921 assessments completed.

11. Target Olympic Podium Scheme – TOPS

The Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) supports elite Indian athletes preparing for major international competitions.

Support includes:

Foreign training
International competitions
Coaching
Equipment
Sports science
Monthly financial support

As of April 2026, TOPS supported 51 Core Athletes, 52 Para Core Athletes and 130 Development Athletes.

12. India's Future Sports Goals

India is also preparing for major future sporting events.

The government has stated the objective of making India:

A top-10 sporting nation by 2036
A top-5 sporting nation by 2047

India has also bid to host the 2036 Olympic Games and is set to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games.

These are future goals/bids, not completed events.
description_te:
Commonwealth Games 2026 – Glasgow

Commonwealth Games 2026 స్కాట్లాండ్‌లోని Glasgowలో 23 July–2 August 2026 మధ్య జరిగాయి.

74 దేశాలు పాల్గొన్నాయి. India తరఫున 124-member contingent పాల్గొంది.

భారతదేశం మొత్తం 39 medals సాధించింది:

13 Gold
17 Silver
9 Bronze

Medal tableలో భారత్ 4వ స్థానంలో నిలిచింది.

2. Mirabai Chanu

Mirabai Chanu Glasgow Commonwealth Gamesలో Gold Medal సాధించింది.

ఇది ఆమెకు వరుసగా మూడవ Commonwealth Games title.

Exam Point:

👉 Mirabai Chanu → Three consecutive Commonwealth Games titles

3. Boxingలో భారత్

Commonwealth Games 2026లో భారత boxers:

7 Gold
3 Silver
10 Total Medals

సాధించారు.

India boxing medal tallyలో మొదటి స్థానంలో నిలిచింది.

Indian women boxersకు ఇది Commonwealth Gamesలో best-ever performanceగా నమోదైంది.

4. Judoలో భారత్

Indian judokas Commonwealth Gamesలో తమ best-ever performance ఇచ్చారు.

భారత్:

2 Gold
1 Silver
1 Bronze

మొత్తం 4 medals సాధించింది.

Asmita Dey మరియు Harsh Singh Commonwealth Games judoలో Indiaకి మొదటి-ever gold medals సాధించారు.

Asmita Dey → Commonwealth Gamesలో Gold గెలిచిన మొదటి Indian woman judoka

Harsh Singh → Gold గెలిచిన మొదటి Indian male judoka.

5. Weightlifting

Indian weightlifters Glasgowలో మొత్తం 8 medals సాధించారు:

1 Gold
6 Silver
1 Bronze

అలాగే Commonwealth records మరియు personal-best performances కూడా నమోదయ్యాయి.

6. Commonwealth Para Games

Indian para-athletes:

3 Gold
2 Silver
2 Bronze

మొత్తం 7 medals సాధించారు.

ఇది Commonwealth Para Gamesలో భారతదేశం సాధించిన best-ever performance.

7. Asian Games 2026

20th Asian Games జపాన్‌లోని Aichi-Nagoyaలో 19 September–4 October 2026 మధ్య జరుగుతున్నాయి.

భారతదేశం 503-member contingentను పంపింది.

వారిలో 300 మందికి పైగా athletes మొదటిసారి Asian Gamesలో పాల్గొంటున్నారు.

8. Jay Meena – Soft Tennis

Jay Meena men's individual Soft Tennisలో Bronze Medal సాధించాడు.

దీంతో అతను Asian Gamesలో Soft Tennis medal సాధించిన మొదటి Indian athlete అయ్యాడు.

Exam Point:

👉 Jay Meena → India's first Asian Games medallist in Soft Tennis

9. Khelo India Expansion

2026లో Union Cabinet expanded Khelo India Schemeకు ఆమోదం తెలిపింది.

Khelo India మరియు National Sports Federationsకు కలిపి:

₹36,441 crore

2026–27 నుంచి 2030–31 వరకు outlay కేటాయించారు.

ముఖ్య లక్ష్యాలు:

Sports infrastructure
Grassroots sports
Athlete development
Talent identification
Training facilities
10. KIRTI

KIRTI = Khelo India Rising Talent Identification

ఇది 9–18 సంవత్సరాల పిల్లల్లో sporting talentను గుర్తించి అభివృద్ధి చేయడానికి ఉద్దేశించబడింది.

AI మరియు data analytics వంటి technologiesను కూడా ఉపయోగిస్తుంది.

2026లో 174 Talent Assessment Centres పనిచేస్తున్నాయి.

11. TOPS

TOPS = Target Olympic Podium Scheme

ఇది elite Indian athletesకు international competitions కోసం support అందిస్తుంది.

ముఖ్యంగా:

Training
Coaching
International competitions
Equipment
Sports science
Financial support

2026 ఏప్రిల్ నాటికి TOPSలో 51 Core Athletes, 52 Para Core Athletes, 130 Development Athletes ఉన్నారు.

12. భారతదేశం భవిష్యత్ క్రీడా లక్ష్యాలు

భారతదేశం:

2036 నాటికి Top-10 sporting nation
2047 నాటికి Top-5 sporting nation

గా ఎదగాలని లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకుంది.

అలాగే India 2036 Olympicsకు hosting bid వేసింది మరియు 2030 Commonwealth Gamesకు ఆతిథ్యం ఇవ్వనుంది.

title: Awards, Appointments, Persons & Places in News
description:
Padma Awards 2026

The Padma Awards are among India's highest civilian honours. They are announced every year on the occasion of Republic Day.

For 2026, the President approved 131 Padma Awards, including 2 duo cases:

Padma Vibhushan – 5
Padma Bhushan – 13
Padma Shri – 113
Women awardees – 19
Posthumous awardees – 16
Foreign/NRI/PIO/OCI awardees – 6

The awards cover fields such as art, literature, education, medicine, science, public affairs, social work, sports and industry.

2. Important Padma Vibhushan Awardees

The five Padma Vibhushan awardees for 2026 included:

Dharmendra Singh Deol – Arts, posthumous
Justice K. T. Thomas – Public Affairs
N. Rajam – Arts
P. Narayanan – Literature and Education
V. S. Achuthanandan – Public Affairs, posthumous

The awards were presented in two Civil Investiture Ceremonies at Rashtrapati Bhavan, on 25 May and 23 June 2026.

3. Important Padma Bhushan Awardees

Among the notable Padma Bhushan awardees in 2026 was Mammootty, recognised for his contribution to Indian cinema.

Other notable recipients included Vellappally Natesan and several personalities from different fields.

Exam Point:
👉 Mammootty → Padma Bhushan 2026

4. Padma Shri and Regional Contributions

The Padma Shri category recognised people from diverse fields and different parts of India.

For example, Prof. Vempaty Kutumba Sastry received the Padma Shri in Literature and Education, while Garimella Balakrishna Prasad received it posthumously in Arts.

This illustrates that Padma Awards recognise not only nationally famous personalities but also individuals contributing at the grassroots level.

5. Supreme Court Appointments

On 1 June 2026, the President approved the appointment of five new judges to the Supreme Court of India.

The appointees were:

Justice Sheel Nagu
Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva
Justice Arun Palli
Venkita Subramani Mohana, Senior Advocate

Exam Point:
👉 Five new Supreme Court judges appointed – June 2026

6. Padma Awards – Basic Classification

For examinations, remember the order:

Padma Vibhushan → Padma Bhushan → Padma Shri

Padma Vibhushan – exceptional and distinguished service
Padma Bhushan – distinguished service of a high order
Padma Shri – distinguished service in any field

The awards were instituted in 1954.

7. People in News – Culture and Cinema

2026 Padma Awards brought several personalities from Indian culture, cinema, literature and traditional arts into the news.

The awards included personalities representing:

Indian classical arts
Cinema
Literature
Education
Traditional knowledge
Social service
Science and technology

This makes the Padma list particularly useful for "Who received which award?" questions.

8. Important Places in News

For competitive exams, places appearing in major national events should be remembered along with their significance.

Rashtrapati Bhavan, New Delhi was particularly important in 2026 because the Padma Awards Civil Investiture Ceremonies were held there.

Glasgow, Scotland was important because it hosted the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Aichi-Nagoya, Japan was important because it hosted the 2026 Asian Games.

These place-event combinations are common examination questions.
